title: Your Virtual Receptionist Just Got a Lot Smarter (And Cheaper)
excerpt: AI receptionists are actually good now, and small businesses are finally asking the right question: do I even need a human answering my phones anymore?

content.text: So there's been this interesting shift happening with virtual receptionists, and I'm genuinely curious what you're going to think about it. For years, the choice was pretty straightforward: hire a real person to answer your phones, or accept that your callers would get a robot that sounds like it was trained on dial-up internet noises. But that's actually changed. Like, noticeably.

AI receptionists have gotten to the point where they can actually do the job. They're handling appointment booking mid-call, they're qualifying leads, they're actually understanding what your customers need without making them repeat themselves three times. And here's the thing nobody wants to admit out loud: for a lot of small businesses, they're working better than the human alternative right now.

items: AI receptionists can now book appointments, take messages, and transfer calls intelligently — not just route 'press 1 for sales'
They're available 24/7 without the payroll headache or time-zone drama
They cost a fraction of what you'd pay for even part-time human coverage
They don't call in sick, ask for raises, or quit to move across the country
But — and this is important — they still can't handle truly complex conversations or angry customers the way a real person can

content.text: A human receptionist costs you $15–25k per year minimum (when you factor in benefits, taxes, and that time they're on break). A good AI receptionist costs $100–500 per month. That's not even a contest mathematically.
The Real Question for Your Business

Here's what you actually need to think about: What percentage of your incoming calls are routine? Schedule an appointment, take a message, answer basic questions about your hours or services? If that's 70% or more of your call volume, an AI receptionist is probably the move. It'll handle those calls in about 10 seconds, free up your team to focus on actual revenue-generating work, and your customers will barely notice the difference.

But if your business is relationship-heavy — if a lot of your calls need someone to actually listen, empathize, and make a judgment call — then a human answering service still wins. Especially for things like medical offices, law practices, or any place where trust matters.

content.label: Intecha's Take
content.text: Don't make this an either/or decision. A lot of businesses are actually doing both now: AI handles your standard calls and off-hours stuff, and you have a human on standby for the calls that actually need a real person. That way you get reliability, cost savings, AND the human touch when it counts. Test-drive an AI option for 30 days. You'll know pretty fast if it's working for your business.
